candidate-30: Every edition compared here contains all of that, word for word. What differs is where verse 14 stops.
Every edition compared here contains that closing material. The numbering difference concerns where verse 14 stops.
Nothing here is a difference in the Greek text at all. It is a difference in how editors divided a text they agree about.

The verse-numbering difference does not remove any of the closing material. There is also a small Greek word-order difference: Nestle places σε before ἰδεῖν, while Robinson–Pierpont and Boyd place it after. That is separate from how the verses are divided.

This is the clearest case in the collection of a difference that is not a textual difference. No word is added, dropped, moved or altered. Two editors drew a line in different places on the same sentence.
The numbering difference itself changes no words. Editors divided the closing material differently; the separate Greek word-order difference does not account for the extra verse number.
